text:
maria: Quick sanity check — after the kernel-chooser autotune landed on canary, we saw weird cache miss spikes. Anyone else?
raj: saw it on two canary hosts. KV miss rate jumped ~4x for short seqs.
jin: link to profiler?
raj: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/2026-03-17/kerntuner-42 — p50 tokens/sec down for seq<=32.
elaine: do we know keying scheme used on the canary driver? Was it the new seq-bin + kernel-tag format?
maria: yes, driver v1.9 writes keys as `model:vhash:kernel_tag:seq_bin` now.
ben: that key composition should be fine, unless vhash changed at model reload?
raj: good point — the model loader also started embedding a build-id into vhash on canary, so model reloads produce new vhash more often.
jin: oh that would invalidate persisted KV entries. Are we persisting across driver restarts?
ops-bot: persistance: kv-store on canary set to `persistent=true`, ttl=null, namespace=prod_canary
ben: so persistent KV + vhash churn = mass misses.
sam: profiling numbers: before change seq<=32 cache hit 87%, after change 21% on same traffic. Long seqs unaffected.
elaine: that aligns with our kernel routing: short seqs tend to use the hot kernel variant; if keys change we lose prefix/KV cache and fallback to kernel that warms slower.
maria: proposed fixes: 1) stop baking build-id into vhash for cache key 2) add key-salt versioning namespace on driver upgrades 3) add ephemeral TTL for short-seq entries while we test. Thoughts?
raj: +1 for namespace versioning. We should be able to migrate without invalidating all entries — use `ns = model_id + ':' + cache_schema_version`.
jin: small counter: namespace versioning is good, but we need to ensure memory usage doesn't spike because duplicates exist during rollout. Maybe ephemeral TTL for the old namespace too?
ben: we measured extra memory ~12% during a similar two-week canary rollout. Might be acceptable but warn infra.
amaria: can we add a graceful fallback that uses partial-key match? e.g., if `model:vhash:kernel:bin` miss, try `model:kernel:bin` (drop vhash) for short sequences only. That avoids full rebuild penalty but needs correctness checks.
elaine: dangerous for cross-model collisions if different models share kernel tag. But scoped to model_id should be ok. We already prefix model_id.
sam: micro-bench: tried `partial-key` fallback in local sim; hit rate recovered to 78% and p50 tokens/sec back to 19ms. But end-to-end quality? need more checks.
maria: action items: (a) rollback build-id-in-vhash change on canary, (b) implement namespace versioning + short TTL for new keys, (c) add partial-key fallback behind flag for seq<=32, (d) run 48h perf and quality run.
raj: I'll open the PR for rollback and namespace API.
jin: I'll run the sim for partial-key fallback and add regression tests to ensure no accidental cross-model leakage.
ben: ops: warn infra about temporary mem bump. Can we run canary at 5% instead of 10% to be safer?
ops-bot: canary route updated to 5% for cluster `us-central-1` by @ben at 2026-03-17T21:12Z
elaine: one more note: batching heuristic interacts — when KV miss spikes, batching falls back to slower path and queueing latency increases. We should monitor queue depth and token wait time metric.
sam: added dashboard panel: `runtime.kv.miss_rate`, `runtime.queue_depth_short_seq`, `runtime.p50_token_wait`.
maria: thanks — let's sync after 48h. If numbers look good we can rollout driver 1.9 with keying changes next week. :thumbsup:
raj: tagging infra and sres for the mem/alerts: @ben @elaine
ops-bot: alert created: `KV_MISS_SPIKE_CANARY` threshold=3x baseline, notify=#eng-oncall
maria: closing loop: big lesson — kernel-autotune changes that touch model identity must be explicit in cache contract. Documenting in this thread for the runbook.
jin: noted, I'll add an entry to runtime/README about key contract and driver upgrade migration steps.
ben: thanks all.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollback redeploy scheduled at 2026-03-17T21:30Z by @raj
